title: Impurity-induced trimer formation across the BCS-BEC crossover
abstract: By means of diffusion Monte Carlo calculations, we study the behavior of a single impurity embedded in two balanced Fermi baths across the BCS-BEC crossover. The impurity interacts attractively with both baths through Pöschl-Teller potentials of different strengths. That interaction is such that does not support an impurity--bath two-body bound state. When that attraction is sufficiently strong, we observe the formation of trimers composed of the impurity and one atom from each bath. These clusters are Borromean on the BCS side, where no two-body subsystem is bound, and evolve continuously into tango-like trimers on the BEC side. Subtracting from the total energy the binding energy of one trimer and that of the remaining bath-bath dimers restores the equation of state of the impurity-free system, supporting a dilute-cluster interpretation. The analysis of interparticle distances shows that the embedded trimer is not simply a dimer dressed by the impurity, but a genuine three-body cluster formed inside the two Fermi baths.
summary: This theoretical study uses Diffusion Monte Carlo simulations to examine how a single impurity affects two interacting Fermi baths as the system transitions from the BCS to the BEC regime. The research demonstrates the formation of stable, genuine three-body clusters (trimers) whose structure changes character across the crossover. This provides crucial insight into multi-body physics beyond simple pair correlations in ultracold atomic gases.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation of impurity-induced trimer clusters as a system of two interacting Fermi baths crosses the BCS-BEC crossover.
main_result: The authors confirm the formation of genuine three-body clusters (trimers) that evolve from Borromean structures on the BCS side to tango-like structures on the BEC side.
method: The primary computational tool used is the Fixed-Node Diffusion Monte Carlo (FN-DMC) method to calculate ground state energies.
model_or_system: The model consists of a single impurity embedded in two balanced Fermi baths, interacting via attractive Pöschl-Teller potentials. The system's behavior is mapped across the BCS-BEC crossover by varying the bath-bath interaction strength.
key_observables: Trimer binding energy ($\epsilon_T$), residual energy ($\Delta E$), and interparticle distances ($\langle r_{ij} angle$).
important_parameters: The BCS-BEC crossover parameter (related to bath-bath interaction strength), and the relative strengths of impurity-bath interactions ($V_{13}$).
main_assumptions: Intra-particle interactions are neglected, and the analysis relies on the fixed-node approximation inherent to the DMC method.
figures_summary: Figures compare total energy vs. interaction strength, showing the effect of the impurity; they also compare isolated trimer energy vs. dimer binding energy, and plot residual energy to confirm the cluster model.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the energy landscape across the crossover, first establishing the general framework using DMC, then focusing on the energy difference ($\Delta E$) to confirm the cluster nature, and finally analyzing the geometry via interparticle distances.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, microscopic understanding of three-body correlations in strongly interacting quantum gases, bridging the gap between simple pairing (dimers) and genuine multi-body physics across a fundamental quantum phase transition.
